text:
eric: Hey, noticed customer ACME is getting negative tokens/sec in the console for the streaming TTFT chart since ~23:00 UTC. Charts show brief dips below zero in 1m rollup windows. Filing here before I open a ticket with infra. :eyes:
mina: Ugh. Do you have an example time range or tenant id?
eric: Yep — org: acme-corp, window samples: 2026-03-15T22:58 -> 2026-03-15T23:07 UTC. See screenshot in the ticket (link). It flips from ~1200 tok/s to -300 for 1 minute then back.
kai: Is this happening across all regions or just us-west-2?
eric: Only us-west-2 for that org, but a handful of other tenants saw tiny negative blips too. Not widespread.
henry: Negative tokens/sec usually means an aggregation delta went negative — maybe rollup counter reset or consumer replayed older offsets. Any Kafka consumer group restarts around then?
mina: Logs show a consumer rebalance at 22:59:14 UTC on metrics-consumer-3 with a subsequent partition reassignment. I'll paste relevant snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T22:59:14Z] INFO consumer-group: rebalance start group=metrics-consumer-3
[2026-03-15T22:59:15Z] WARN leader-change partition=12 oldLeader=broker-7 newLeader=broker-2
[2026-03-15T22:59:16Z] INFO offset-commit failed partition=12 err=OffsetOutOfRange
```
henry: OffsetOutOfRange is a red flag — if the consumer seeks to an earlier offset or replays, the rollup delta computation can go negative if the checkpoint wasn't reset.
kai: Can we repro locally by simulating an offset rewind + our rollup pipeline? If yes I can run a repro on staging.
eric: I pulled a small payload dump for partition 12 and reprocessed it locally; I see the same delta inversion when I replay a batch where the stored last_count > current_count due to an older partial write then a full write.
mina: Theory: we aggregate tokens/sec by taking post-agg cumulative counters (monotonic) and diffing. If a partial write with lower cumulative value is processed after a higher value (due to out-of-order), diff becomes negative for that window. We should clamp negative diffs to 0 or use last-known-good. But that may mask real regressions.
henry: Short-term fix: clamp negatives to 0 at the visualization layer to avoid billing/alert noise. Long-term: make the rollup idempotent by using committed offsets + checkpoint TTL and discard replays older than checkpoint timestamp.
era metrics-bot: Detected anomalous negative deltas for tokens/sec on acme-corp at 2026-03-15T22:59:00Z, magnitude -312 tok/s, partitions [12,17].
eric: Workaround for ACME customers: switch their console to 'per-shard' metric view (not aggregated) — that hides window-level negative deltas. Can we enable that as a temporary toggle?
kai: I can patch the console to clamp negatives for the dashboard only and roll to canary in prod. PR will be small.
mina: Meanwhile I'll open a ticket with infra to check consumer group flapping and if compaction/retention on the topic could produce OffsetOutOfRange. Might need to increase retention or reconfigure offsets.
henry: Also check the checkpoint store (etcd) — if writes were delayed and the consumer resumed at an earlier checkpoint, that could explain it.
eric: Assigning: kai (console clamp), mina (consumer + topic retention), henry (checkpoint + rollback detection). I'll coordinate with ACME support and send a status note.
kai: Starting console fix: clamping negative diffs to 0 in visualization and adding a tooltip explaining it. Deploying to canary now. :construction:
metrics-bot: Deploy started: canary-console-2026-03-16T00:15Z by kai.
kai: Canary looks good, negatives disappeared in canary dashboard for the same time range. No regressions seen. Rolling to 10% tomorrow morning.
mina: Infra found brief retention misconfig on metrics topic; retention_ms temporarily short-circuited during infra maintenance at 22:58:45 UTC — some offsets became unavailable and consumers sought to earliest. Raising retention to 7d and adding alert on retention-ms changes.
henry: Checkpoint store had 2 delayed commits around 22:58:50Z due to a transient etcd leader election. I added idempotency: if incoming cumulative counter < last_seen and timestamp < last_seen_ts then ignore; if timestamp >= last_seen_ts allow and clamp else flag for manual review. Patch posted.
eric: Good. For ACME I'll mark this as mitigated — console clamp + infra retention fix + checkpoint idempotency in pipeline.
mina: Suggest follow-up: run a consumer replay test and a simulated leader-election to verify no further negative deltas for any tenant. I'll schedule it.
kai: After canary completes, I'll add a lightweight alert to detect repeated negative windows (>3 windows in 10m) and auto-open an incident.
eric: Thanks all. I'll send ACME incident update: short-term mitigation applied, engineering working root cause (infrastructure retention + checkpoint race) and plan to harden pipeline.
metrics-bot: Incident note created: INC-20260315-0791 linked to thread 2356789012.
eric: Closing thread once postmortem doc is uploaded. Will ping when PM writes the note. :thumbsup:
